newsitem.title: USA: Judge mulls Los Angeles agency, Lazard Freres case.
newsitem.headline: Judge mulls Los Angeles agency, Lazard Freres case.

text.p: A judge Friday decided to take under consideration Lazard Freres & Co's motion to dismiss a Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority municipal bond suit, attorney said.

On Thursday, the Superior Court judge issued a tentative ruling that favored the authority. But in court Friday, after hearing oral arguments, he decided to take the matter under submission, attorneys said. He was expected to rule on the motion in the coming days.
Lazard Freres maintains the suit should be dismissed because it was not served within the required time period.

In April, the Los Angeles authority sued Lazard Freres, joining a suit by former investment banker Michael Lissack. The lawsuit, which seeks at least $14 million, was filed in California Superior Court under the California False Claims Act, a law providing financial incentives to whistleblowers.
Lazard Freres, which dropped out of the municipal industry in December, but maintains a financial advisory unit, has denied any wrongdoing.
"We don't think we did anything wrong," Lazard Freres attorney Steven Schatz said Friday.
The lawsuit alleged Lazard Freres overcharged the Los Angeles authority by more than $3 million on a purchase of $542 million of Treasuries used in a 1993 bond deal.
The county paid Lazard Freres $1.8 million over three years to serve as its financial adviser on bond deals, including the 1993 refunding.
Under the False Claims Act, the county can recover three times the damages, which includes the $3 million alleged overcharge and the $1.8 million advisory fee, the suit said.
The suit also alleged that Lazard Freres breached its fiduciary duty, breached its contract and violated sections of the state civil and government codes.
The suit, though filed in Los Angeles, has been transferred to San Francisco.
